container: Nanotechnology offers tools for building materials and devices at extremely small scales. It can improve medicine by delivering drugs directly to diseased cells, detecting illness earlier, and supporting precise treatments. Tiny coatings may make surfaces stronger, lighter, and resistant to water or bacteria. In electronics, nanomaterials can enable faster, smaller components, while improved batteries and solar cells may support cleaner energy. However, nanoparticles can behave unpredictably and enter air, water, or living tissue. Their long term health and environmental effects are not fully understood. Careful testing, regulation, and oversight are essential to protect people and ecosystems.
